About the role
We are looking for a talented and motivated Research Associate to join the Alloy Design & Phase Transformations Research Group in the School of Engineering at the University of Leicester. You will contribute to a research project funded through an EPSRC New Investigator Award, developing a new generation of austenitic steels with exceptionally low thermal expansion while maintaining mechanical strength and structural stability at elevated temperatures. Working closely with academic and industrial collaborators, you will combine experimental metallurgy, computational modelling and machine learning to investigate how alloy composition, processing and magnetic phase stability influence material performance, with potential applications spanning advanced power generation, aerospace, fusion energy and defence.
You will take a leading role in the design, production and heat-treatment of new steel alloys, integrating experimental findings with thermodynamic and data-driven modelling to guide alloy development. Your research will involve thermal expansion and magnetic measurements, X-ray diffraction, SEM, TEM and EBSD, alongside high-temperature tensile, creep and fatigue testing.
You will have access to specialist research infrastructure, including Leicester's Hercules Facility, which specialises in correlative 3D materials characterisation through complementary X-ray and electron microscopy techniques across multiple length scales. You will work closely with collaborators at the Henry Royce Institute and Marcegaglia Stainless Sheffield Ltd and contribute to high-quality scientific publications, international conferences and knowledge exchange with industrial partners.
About you
You will have, or be close to completing, a PhD in materials science, metallurgy, materials engineering, mechanical engineering or a related discipline, or have equivalent research experience. You will bring research experience of metallic alloys and practical experience in at least one relevant characterisation or testing technique, such as SEM, EBSD, TEM, X-ray diffraction, dilatometry or high-temperature mechanical testing. You will also have experience in quantitative data analysis and scientific programming or modelling using Python, MATLAB or equivalent tools, together with the ability to design experiments, interpret complex datasets and understand relationships between processing, structure and material properties.
You will be able to plan and undertake research independently while contributing effectively within a multidisciplinary team, communicating complex technical findings clearly to academic and industrial audiences. You will bring sound analytical judgement, a careful approach to experimental work and a commitment to accurate, reproducible research. Experience of machine learning or statistical modelling applied to materials data, computational thermodynamics, magnetic characterisation, advanced microscopy or high-temperature creep and fatigue testing would be particularly valuable, as would previous experience of collaborative academic-industry research.
Additional information

Informal enquiries are welcomed and should be directed to Dr Gebril El-Fallah at gmae2@leicester.ac.uk

We anticipate that interviews will take place mid-January 2027.
 
As part of the University’s ongoing commitment to professional development, this role will also be considered on a seconded basis for existing staff members. Please ensure this is discussed with your line manager prior to applying. More information regarding secondments can be found here.

We’re committed to the wellbeing of all our staff and to the sustainability of our environment, on our campus and beyond. Role Description

We welcome applications from skilled researchers to join us and help to develop resilient radio frequency receiver systems for alternative Positioning, Navigation and Timing.

About the Role

This practical role brings together antenna configuration, commercial off-the-shelf radio frequency front-end prototyping, software-defined radio and digital signal processing. The successful candidate will design, integrate and experimentally evaluate commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) based radio frequency receivers, selecting and configuring antennas, front-end components and software-defined radio (SDR) data acquisition platforms. Initially focusing on terrestrial alternative Positioning, Navigation and Timing (PNT) applications, such as eLoran, you will investigate how antenna type, orientation, placement and diversity affect the resilience of signal reception.

The work will include exploring antenna configuration effects on receiver dynamic range and local interference, and the potential of combining signals from multiple receiving channels. You will develop and test digital signal processing methods for signal acquisition and tracking, interference analysis, adaptive filtering and jamming/spoofing detection, with opportunities to develop and apply suitable AI/ML techniques too. Simulation and laboratory results will be evaluated through field measurements and controlled, compliant interference experiments, using Cranfield’s PNT and radio frequency facilities, and working alongside academic and industrial partners.

About You

We welcome applications from individuals with a range of relevant radio frequency backgrounds, including HF/VHF communications, cellular systems and radio frequency sensing. You will have a PhD (or close to completion) in Electrical or Electronic Engineering, Communications, Radio Frequency Engineering, Signal Processing, Embedded Systems or a related discipline. You will bring practical experience of integrating or evaluating radio frequency receiving systems using SDR platforms or COTS hardware, supported by radio frequency measurement experience and a general understanding of antennas and receiver front-end fundamentals. You will also have practical signal processing experience in signal detection, analysis, estimation or filtering.

A completed PhD focused on radio frequency receiver systems, SDR, signal processing for sensing or PNT, or resilient radio frequency communications would be an advantage. Experience with antenna diversity, A-PNT, AI/ML for signal processing, or embedded/real-time receiver development is welcome.

You will be comfortable programming in Python, MATLAB and/or C/C++, processing live or recorded radio frequency data, using radio frequency/electronics laboratory equipment, and interpreting experimental results. You will be able to plan reproducible measurements, document your work, and communicate your findings through technical reports, publications or presentations. You will enjoy hands-on experimentation while collaborating across hardware, software and algorithm disciplines. Experience with FPGA/GPU optimisation, antenna modelling or automated instrumentation would be beneficial.

About Us

As a specialist postgraduate university, Cranfield’s world-class expertise, large-scale facilities and unrivalled industry partnerships are creating leaders in technology and management globally. Learn more about Cranfield and our unique impact here.

Aerospace is at the heart of Cranfield’s global research airport and is renowned throughout the world for its teaching and research in the fields of Aviation and Aerospace. Cranfield Aerospace’s six Centres are the powerhouses of our world-class research, driving technological and conceptual advances in aeronautics, propulsion engineering, cyber-physical systems and intelligent automation. Through the strong links with industry built over the past 70 years, we focus on defining and delivering the aircraft, airport and airspace management of the future, and are the only university in Europe with our own airport and runway. Cranfield Aerospace is internationally recognised as the first choice for research and education in all aspects of aerospace, including aircraft, drones, urban air mobility and space. Find out more about our work here.

Our Values and Commitments

Our shared, stated values help to define who we are and underpin everything we do: Ambition; Impact; Respect; and Community. Find out more here.

We aim to create and maintain a culture in which everyone can work and study together and realise their full potential. We are a Disability Confident Employer. We are committed to actively exploring flexible working options for each role and have been ranked in the Top 30 family friendly employers in the UK by the charity Working Families. Find out more about our key commitments to Equality, Diversity and Inclusion and Flexible Working here.

Working Arrangements

Collaborating and connecting are integral to so much of what we do. Our Working Arrangements Framework provides many staff with the opportunity to flexibly combine on-site and remote working, where job roles allow, balancing the needs of our community of staff, students, clients and partners.

How to apply                                   

For an informal discussion about this opportunity, please contact Professor Ivan Petrunin, Professor of Signal Processing and Intelligent Systems, on (T): +44 (0) 1234 750111 Ext. 8262, or (E): i.petrunin@cranfield.ac.uk

Apply online now. Please do not hesitate to contact us for further details on (E): peoplerecruitment@cranfield.ac.uk. Please quote reference number 5441.

Closing date for receipt of applications:   10 January 2027

Please note that we reserve the right to close this advert prior to the stated closing date should we receive sufficient numbers of applications. Therefore, we would encourage you to complete and submit your application as soon as possible.

As a Research Associate, you will lead the development of a multiscale virtual asthma patient within the UKRI Future Leaders Fellowship programme, the Lung Pharmacome. You will bring together mechanistic modelling with multimodal biological and clinical data and experimental evidence from patient-derived lung organoids, helping to improve understanding of asthma heterogeneity and treatment response. Working across computational, experimental, clinical and engineering disciplines, you will develop, calibrate and validate transparent and testable computational models and reproducible modelling and data-analysis workflows.
This is an interdisciplinary and outward-facing research role in which you will provide intellectual leadership for the virtual-patient workstream while working closely with the Principal Investigator, the Research Associate leading the lung-organoid platform, and collaborators spanning respiratory science, clinical research, engineering, data science and enterprise. You will contribute to publications and wider dissemination, mentor students and less-experienced researchers, build collaborations, and help translate the research towards practical application and commercialisation, including engagement with patients, industry partners and other external stakeholders.

You will have a PhD, or have submitted your thesis by the time of appointment, in computational biology, systems biology, bioengineering, biomedical data science, quantitative biomedicine, bioinformatics or a closely related discipline. You will be comfortable working independently while contributing collaboratively across disciplinary boundaries, with strong analytical judgement, communication and project organisation skills. About the role

This is an excellent opportunity for a postdoctoral researcher to develop their research career in Human Factors and translational healthcare research within a dynamic and multidisciplinary environment.

You will join the core methodology team within the NIHR HealthTech Research Centre for In Vitro Diagnostics (HRC IVD) at Imperial College London. The role will contribute to a growing Human Factors research programme focused on understanding and improving the interaction between people, technologies and healthcare systems, supporting the safe, effective and successful development and implementation of diagnostic technologies and medical devices.

Working across multidisciplinary research programmes, the post-holder will apply Human Factors principles and methodologies to investigate usability, human–technology interaction, task performance, clinical workflows, use errors and system-level factors influencing the adoption and implementation of healthcare technologies. The role will involve designing and delivering qualitative, quantitative and mixed-methods research, translating findings into practical recommendations and contributing to the development of evidence-based approaches to Human Factors evaluation in healthcare.

You will work closely with clinicians, engineers, scientists, researchers, industry partners and patient and public contributors, contributing to research that supports innovation and the translation of healthcare technologies into clinical practice.

Essential requirements include a PhD in Human Factors/Ergonomics, Psychology, Healthcare Technology, or a related discipline. Experience in designing and conducting research involving human participants, together with knowledge of qualitative and quantitative or quantitative research methods, is essential. Experience applying Human Factors principles within healthcare, medical devices, diagnostics or other complex socio-technical environments would be highly desirable.

The College is supportive of flexible working. The Department is happy to discuss the possibility of implementing such arrangements for this post, with suitably qualified people, subject to operational requirements.

What you would be doing

As a Research Associate/ Research Fellow in Human Factors at the NIHR HealthTech Research Centre in IVD, you will design, conduct and contribute to high-quality Human Factors research across a portfolio of translational healthcare research programmes.

You will investigate how people interact with healthcare technologies and how individual, task-related, environmental and organisational factors influence usability, safety, performance, and implementation. You will apply qualitative, quantitative and mixed-methods approaches, including usability evaluation, task and workflow analysis, observational research, interviews, surveys, focus groups, experimental studies and Human Factors risk assessment.

Working within a multidisciplinary research environment, you will translate human factors findings into evidence-based recommendations to inform technology design, optimisation, clinical workflows, training and implementation strategies. You will also contribute to research publications, funding applications, stakeholder engagement, and the continuing development of our research capability.

The role will provide opportunities to develop methodological expertise and introduce innovative research approaches.

What we are looking for

We are looking for a motivated and adaptable researcher with a strong interest in Human Factors and its application to healthcare technology development and implementation.

The successful candidate will demonstrate:

A PhD in Human Factors/Ergonomics, Psychology, Healthcare Technology or a related discipline.
Knowledge of Human Factors principles, particularly human–technology interaction, usability, task performance, and socio-technical systems.
Experience designing, conducting and analysing research involving human participants, users, technologies, or processes.
Experience in both qualitative and quantitative research or, solely, qualitative research methodologies.
Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills, including the ability to identify underlying human, technological and system-level factors influencing performance and outcomes.
Ability to translate Human Factors research findings into practical, evidence-based recommendations for improving technology design, usability, safety and implementation.
Strong research skills, including study design, data collection, analysis, scientific writing, and dissemination of research findings.
Ability to work independently, take initiative, and manage multiple research activities within agreed timelines.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively within multidisciplinary teams and engage with academic, clinical, technical and non-academic stakeholders.
A proactive and adaptable approach, with an interest in developing new methodologies, exploring emerging technologies and contributing to the growth of the Human Factors research programme.
Experience in simulation-based research or behavioral measurement would be advantageous. Experience in healthcare, medical devices, diagnostic technologies, or translational research would also be desirable.

 

What we can offer you

The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to continue science for humanity.
Grow your career: gain access to Imperial’s leading dedicated career support for researchers as well as opportunities for promotion and progression.
Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 43 days off a year and generous pension schemes).
Be part of a diverse, inclusive, and collaborative work culture with various staff networks and resources to support your personal and professional wellbeing.

Further information

This is a full-time post for 12 months in the first instance, based at Hammersmith Hospital and White City Campus, London.

If you require any further details about the role, please contact:

Professor Peter Buckle – p.buckle@imperial.ac.uk

We are looking for a Research Assistant to join the Division of Molecular and Cell Biology and the Leicester Institute of Structural and Chemical Biology (LISCB), working on a Wellcome-funded project led by Dr Yolanda Markaki. The project investigates X chromosome inactivation (XCI) and X-linked gene regulation in embryonic stem cells. You will culture and differentiate human pluripotent stem cells, undertake RNA FISH and immunofluorescence, use super-resolution fluorescence microscopy and Fiji for image analysis, and develop and apply RNA-seq workflows within a high-performance computing environment. The project forms part of Wellcome-funded research investigating how cells switch off genes during early development, with the potential to advance understanding of gene silencing and developmental disorders. 

You will analyse and interpret experimental and transcriptomic data, including differential expression and allele-specific expression, and integrate this with information on XCI classification, genomic position and transcription factors. You will maintain accurate and reproducible laboratory and data records, communicate findings through lab meetings, conferences, publications and funder reports, and contribute to the wider success of the research programme, including providing day-to-day guidance to project students where appropriate. About you
You will hold an MSc in Bioinformatics and have experience of culturing embryonic stem cells and working with differentiation models. You will have practical experience of RNA FISH, immunofluorescence, advanced fluorescence microscopy and image analysis using Fiji, alongside experience of developing and applying RNA-seq workflows to investigate X chromosome inactivation and X-linked gene regulation in human pluripotent stem cells. You will also be experienced in using high-performance computing environments for read alignment, BAM processing, variant calling and allele-specific analysis. 

You will be skilled in differential expression analysis, X-linked gene annotation and allele-specific expression analysis, with the ability to integrate transcriptomic datasets with published XCI classifications and other genomic information. Proficiency in R, statistical analysis and reproducible bioinformatics workflows is essential, as are strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work effectively both independently and collaboratively. Experience of presenting research findings is desirable, as is familiarity with workflow managers such as Snakemake or Nextflow and version control such as Git.

About the role
We are looking for a talented Research Assistant to join the Division of Molecular and Cell Biology and Leicester Institute of Structural and Chemical Biology (LISCB) at the University of Leicester. This full-time, fixed-term role, available until 31 March 2029, is funded by Wellcome and will contribute to research led by Dr Yolanda Markaki investigating how X chromosome inactivation (XCI) and heterochromatin formation are regulated during early embryonic development. The wider Wellcome-funded programme explores how cells switch off genes during early development, using advanced super-resolution microscopy to understand the molecular interactions involved in X chromosome silencing. 

You will use mouse embryonic stem cells and developmental models alongside CRISPR genome editing, quantitative super-resolution microscopy, protein biochemistry, molecular biology and epigenomic approaches. You will analyse and integrate imaging, biochemical and genomic data, working with the Principal Investigator to develop new hypotheses and experimental approaches. You will also contribute to publications and reports, present findings at laboratory meetings and national and international conferences, and provide day-to-day guidance to project students. Dr Yolanda Markaki’s research focuses on developmental epigenetics and nuclear architecture, including X chromosome inactivation, heterochromatin formation and quantitative super-resolution imaging.
About you
You will have a PhD, awarded or close to submission, in stem cell biology, cell and molecular biology, biochemistry or a related discipline, together with relevant research experience in X chromosome inactivation and the regulation of heterochromatin formation during early embryonic development. You will bring experience of mouse embryonic stem cells and developmental models, super-resolution microscopy, RNA and DNA FISH, quantitative image analysis using Fiji, RNAseq, protein biochemistry and molecular biology techniques, including chromatin immunoprecipitation and Cut&Run. You will also have knowledge of epigenetic regulation during early embryonic development, particularly the function of HDAC1, HDAC2 and HDAC3 complexes, and familiarity with CRISPR genome editing. 

Able to design, undertake and troubleshoot experiments independently, you will be an effective communicator who can organise and prioritise your work while contributing positively to a collaborative research environment. Experience of guiding students, analysing imaging or genomics data using Fiji, R or Python, publishing in peer-reviewed journals or presenting at conferences would be advantageous. 

Additional information
For informal enquiries, please contact Dr Yolanda Markaki on yolanda.markaki@leicester.ac.uk. 
 
As part of the University’s ongoing commitment to professional development, this role will also be considered on a seconded basis for existing staff members. Please ensure this is discussed with your line manager prior to applying. More information regarding secondments can be found here 
 
The University of Leicester has been changing the world, and changing people’s lives, for 100 years. When you join us, you’ll become part of a community of Citizens of Change, which includes not only our staff and our current students but also thousands of Leicester graduates around the world.
 
As a diverse and forward-thinking employer, we embed the principles of equity, diversity and inclusion into everything we do. That includes not just our core missions of teaching and research, but also our support for staff, students and our local community through our values of Inspiring, Impactful and Inclusive.
 
We’re committed to the wellbeing of all our staff and to the sustainability of our environment, on our campus and beyond. We offer a competitive salary package, excellent pension scheme and a generous annual leave allowance, along with opportunities to develop your career in a supportive and collaborative environment.

Job Title: Research Fellow

Reference:  622             

Department: WMS - Biomedical Sciences

Contract Type: Fixed-term contract

Fixed Term End Date: 10 January 2028

Hours: Full-time (1.0 FTE)

Closing Date: Monday 14 December 2026, 11:59pm (UK)                     

Full time Salary Range: £37,369  - £46,970 per annum

About the Role

To deliver an industry-funded, translational programme investigating the biological mechanisms underlying endometriosis. The post holder will undertake a combination of human and preclinical research, integrating patient-derived samples, clinical data and experimental models to generate insight into disease pathophysiology. They will work closely with the academic team and industry funder to generate robust, decision-quality data, and communicate progress against agreed milestones.

 

For details on the experience and skills required, please refer to the job description (link here).

About You

We are seeking a highly motivated and dedicated individual with a strong background in immunology and experience in disease modelling, flow cytometry, bulk sequencing and computational biology, including computational analysis using R/Python. Holding a Home Office Personal Licence (PIL) would be desirable.

This role forms part of a collaborative research project with industry. The successful candidate should demonstrate a strong work ethic, scientific rigour, initiative and excellent organisational skills, with a commitment to delivering high-quality, milestone-driven research within agreed timelines. The ability to work independently and collaboratively with both academic and industry partners is essential.

If you are near submission of your PhD, or have not yet had it conferred, any offers of employment will be made at Research Assistant level, at the highest spinal point of pay grade 5. Upon receipt of evidence confirming the successful award of your PhD, you will be promoted to Research Fellow, at the lowest spinal point of grade 6.

About the Department

Warwick Medical School has an excellent reputation for our distinctive portfolio of high-quality education programmes and for the excellence and global impact of our research. 

The breadth of our interest and expertise is demonstrated through our dynamic and influential directorates: Warwick Applied Health (WAH), Warwick Clinical Trials Unit (WCTU), and Warwick Biomedical Sciences (BMS).  Our Institute of Translational Medicine (ITM) works across the directorates, University and with external stakeholders to accelerate the delivery of practical human health benefits arising from research. 

Warwick Biomedical Science's mission is to advance world-class discovery science with an interdisciplinary approach to unravel the fundamental mechanisms of physiological and pathological processes; develop pioneering diagnostic and preventative technologies; and deliver ground-breaking treatments for a healthier future for all. 

 

Our research is grouped into the following disciplines: 

Cell and Mechano-Biology Discovery research with a focus on cytoskeletal self-organisation, membrane dynamics and tissue mechanobiology. Investigators in this theme form the core of the University-wide Centre for Mechanochemical Cell Biology. 

Host-Pathogen Interactions Discovery research and innovation focussing on pathogenicity factors and host machinery involved in infection and new approaches in diagnosis, prevention and immunity. 

Reproductive Biomedicine Discovery, translational and clinical research into gametogenesis, implantation, miscarriage, endometriosis, labour and birth with investigators forming the core of the Centre for Early Life and cross-cutting WMS programme in Women's Health. 

 

Our cross-cutting initiatives include: 

Research and innovation in bioinformatics, chrono medicine and nanoparticle-based drug delivery. 

Translational and clinical research into metabolic disorders, pathology, cardiology and surgery. 

WMS offers academic education across several levels and is the UK leader for graduate entry medicine.  Our portfolio of postgraduate programmes aims to provide excellent education and continued professional development for healthcare professionals across a number of areas, including advanced clinical and critical care practice, diabetes, leadership, medical education, interdisciplinary biomedical research, public health and health research.  We have expanded our education portfolio to include two innovative undergraduate courses: MSci Integrated Natural Sciences and BSc Health and Medical Sciences.  We also offer full and part time research degrees either at Warwick Medical School or in a clinical setting, encompassing PhDs, MD Doctor of Medicine, PhD by Published Work, and MSc by Research. 

We foster a rich and inclusive education and research eco-system, underpinned by our core values which permeate everything we do: Integrity, Collaboration, Respect, Excellence, Innovation and Efficiency, and Courage. 

The Medical School and University exist within a local, regional, national and international health and care diaspora with excellent inter-institutional links, partnerships and relationships.  The connections stretch across academia, industry and the NHS, with a particular strength in our local health eco-system with our local NHS trusts.  The strong and effective relationships that we have established over the past 25 years support our excellent teaching, research, innovation and broader educational and academic activities and enable new and existing activities to be undertaken to the highest of standards.

How to Apply

To apply please complete your essential personal details and attach a CV and cover letter by the closing date stated. 

 

We will review applications throughout the advertising period and may contact shortlisted candidates before the closing date. We therefore encourage interested applicants to submit their application as early as possible. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early should we receive a sufficient number of suitable applications.

 

Please ensure your CV includes your most recent employment experience along with any additional relevant experience and education history.

 

Your cover letter should detail your motivation for applying for the role as well as detailing how you meet the essential and desirable criteria.   

 

The interviews will be held on a date to be confirmed. 

We will provide you with a great range of benefits, which include an attractive pension scheme, a generous holiday allowance plus Christmas closure, excellent learning and development opportunities, and savings on a wide range of products and services. We offer a generous maternity/paternity/adoption/parental leave policy, and onsite childcare facilities.

 

We recognise the importance of a healthy work/life balance and offer you access to flexible working, for more information click here.

 

We are proud to say that we are a Living Wage employer.

 

If you are considering relocating to the UK, read our Relocation Guide to find out more about what Warwick has to offer and what might be involved in the process.

 

Warwick is committed to building an organisation of mutual respect and dignity, promoting a welcoming, diverse, and inclusive working and learning environment.  We recognise that everyone is different in a variety of visible and non-visible ways, and that those differences are to be recognised, respected, and valued.  Where possible, we go beyond legislation to provide a place where everyone can thrive, supporting all staff to achieve their full potential. We aspire to remove economic, social, and cultural barriers that may otherwise prevent people from succeeding.

 

We therefore welcome and encourage applications from all communities regardless of culture, background, age, disability, sex/gender, gender identity or expression, ethnicity, religion/belief, or sexual or romantic orientation. To find out more about our social inclusion work at Warwick visit our webpages here.

 

The University currently holds a Race Equality Charter Bronze Award, Athena Swan Sliver Award and a Disability Smart Bronze Award. Further information on all of the University's Awards and Accreditations can be found here. The University of Warwick is also one of the six founder institutions of the EUTOPIA European University Alliance.

About the Role

Metal manufacturing is a complex, multi-stage activity in which the processing route – casting, rolling, forging, heat treatment and forming – determines the microstructure and therefore the final properties of the product. Finite element (FE) modelling is widely used to predict temperatures, strains and loads during processing, but these models are rarely linked to the underlying metallurgy, such as recrystallisation, grain growth, phase transformation and precipitation. Where coupled process–metallurgy models do exist, they are often bespoke, difficult to reuse and not readily accessible to industry, particularly SMEs, or to students and early-career engineers. There is a clear need for a shared, validated set of models that connect processing conditions to microstructure and properties, helping industry to reduce costly trials and supporting the education of the next generation of metallurgists and modellers.

This project will create a library of COMSOL Multiphysics models for key metal manufacturing processes, combining finite element simulation with core metallurgical concepts. You will build a set of robust, well-documented foundation models – for example for hot rolling, heat treatment and forming – that couple thermal, mechanical and microstructural behaviour, and validate them against experimental and industrial data. The models are intended to be shared with industry and used in education, so a key part of the role will be making them accessible to non-specialists through clear documentation, worked examples and teaching material. You will work closely with industrial partners, SMEs and other academic institutions to identify priority processes, gather process data and develop case studies, ensuring the library addresses real industrial needs while providing a lasting resource for training and teaching.

 

For details on the experience and skills required, please refer to the job description (link here). 

About You

You will hold a PhD and have already demonstrated both excellence and independence in research.  You will have a track record of internationally recognised publications in metallurgy, manufacturing modelling or material science, and have expertise in finite element modelling using ideally COMSOL, but other software experience will be considered. We are looking for a COMSOL modeller to join our team. Supported by experienced metallurgists, you will help develop these new models and ensure they are easy to use for both industry and students.

We are seeking candidates who can make a strong contribution to both our research both directly through the project but also to the broader group, and who will make the most of the opportunities provided by our lively and vibrant departmental culture.

If you are near submission of your PhD, or have not yet had it conferred, any offers of employment will be made at Research Assistant level, at the highest spinal point of pay grade 5. Upon receipt of evidence confirming the successful award of your PhD, you will be promoted to Research Fellow, at the lowest spinal point of grade 6.

About the Department

WMG is the largest department at the University of Warwick, with over 800 staff and nearly 3,000 students across undergraduate and postgraduate programmes in management, technology, and applied engineering.

We are globally recognised for our world-class research, innovative industry partnerships, and teaching excellence, and we are proud holders of the Athena SWAN Silver Award and the Institutional Silver Award.
